body: Doesn't look right. I'll check it.
The assumption of validating multiple files is that the files are indexed by integers. In your case, you should validate each individual file upload separately.

I don't understand what is wrong with custom indexes.
And if I use integer indexes like you say, the problem is still here

```
...
<?= $form->field($model, 'file[5]')->dropDownList($items1) ?>
<?= $form->field($model, 'file[9]')->dropDownList($items2) ?>
...
```

Will become after validation : 

```
[
    0 => yii\web\UploadedFile ...
    1 => yii\web\UploadedFile ...
]
```

I don't want attributes _file_custom1_ and _file_custom2_, I need an array.

@timmy78, totally agree with you. Its... Vary annoying. Why should it be like this?
As an option, you can save state before validation and restore it thereafter

This behavior is questionable indeed. I checked the current tests (FileValidatorTest) and these do not cover this particular part of the code https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/validators/FileValidator.php#L200

issue.title: Fixed changing array keys after validation of multiple files in yii\validators\FileValidator
